[pre]Beyond the Canglu Plains flank two lakes. Gaze at the water and listen carefully to a somber song. The lakes never stop singing. Every night as you lay in bed, listen carefully, then unconsciously, the voices become greater and more numerous. In the darkest night the lakes still into a plate of solid gold underneath the star-lit sky and illuminates the world and voice is the heavenly queen. They never stop singing. We are roused and walk across the sands and stand with our feet deep within the water hyacinths to meet our performers but in the daybreak the singing dissipates but does not end. Gaze at the water and listen carefully. With your head against the surface of the world, the song is still there.[/pre]

[spoiler=The House of the Plate of Gold][b]House of the Plate of Gold[/b]

It was the early morning, though the two had been in transit far before midnight, riding inside a driverless van. They only made two stops in the outskirts of the Canglu Plains, one at a QP gas station to refill the  van, then another station for relief and cookies. The pair were driven along the forlorn highway and reached a great wall of steel and concrete, lined along its midsection with lights, sniper nests, and sensors forbidding intruders from even creating the thought of entering without its mighty sanction.

[list]

"Very dark tonight, Comrade Zhang." The man said, his eyes roaming through the little white dots that emanated out of the astronomical aether. "Ever walked underneath a night sky and gotten lost? Western folks will just laugh at you and say to look at the light. As in, all the horrible light pollution generated by their decadent cities. Here though, it is only dark nights and luminous mornings."

"It's just the boundary region, Comrade Cui. The only stretch of land humanity has colonized here is the road we're on." The woman brusquely replied, humoring her gruff colleague, half-distracted by messages coming in from her phone.

"Well still. Come on, you get what I mean Comrade. Have you seen Western cities? They're horrible. Sometimes you can't even tell what time of day it was with all the bright signs and the noise. And the skyscrapers, those castles made out of glass. What use were spires pursuing the heaven when heaven itself could be found on equal ground?"

"5G transceivers I guess." The woman retorted. "We still need a connection for heaven on equal ground."

"You university folk have no regard for the beauty of socialism."

"Am I being threatened?"

"Just critiqued. I don't talk to people I wish to threaten, Comrade Zhang."

[/list]

The driverless van stopped as it reached the tunnel leading through the wall. The man a woman step out of the van and raised their arms in a T-shape as guardsmen at the checkpoint walked up to check them for any illegal paraphernalia, then their car. License and registration, insurance, party ID, entry tickets, these were all submitted in quick succession thereafter.

The man was a towering figure, mighty enough to urge the guards to speak with courtesy. That, or maybe the MZP tags on his military uniform commanded more authority. Medium black hair, sun-kissed skin that seemed fairer at a distance, a gaunt and heavy expression. The man was Cui Jin, a member of the MZP Central Committee and formerly of the Red Army Commission, now the incoming party secretary for the University of Qianxun following a recent administrative reshuffle at the Politburo.

Next to him, a bespectacled woman named Zhang Meihui, who formed part of the University of Qianxun's faculty. She was usually seen in a lab coat, though that night she wore a grey and white blouse and trousers. Her short hair was cut roughly towards her shoulder, with a color resembling bronze, or at least the midway between brown and auburn, with jade-colored eyes and fair skin. She had been assigned to serve as Cui Jin's guide to the university, an assignment she greatly detested for but one reason.

[list]

"Why did they even assign you as party secretary? You don't even have the slightest clue about the university's affairs." Zhang quietly zapped at Cui just as the guards finish frisking her. "Sincerely, I think I'll give you two months tops before you reassigned to the Red Guards Bureau."

"Am I being critiqued?"

"No, just threatened."

[/list]

Finally, the guards clear the two for entry and they are led back into the van, which automatically hums back to life upon confirming that both of its registered passengers were seated. The barriers upon, and the van began driving through the tunnel of the great exterior wall. They had not been in the Canglu Plains for a time, but as they exit the tunnel it was clear now that they were now in a world that was different from the last. Qianxun Lakes.

The roads continued, then thinned, and then were gone as the van turned right onto a massive parking lot that preceded another immense row of walls. Not the same sort of walls constructed from tyrannical concrete and steel, but instead beautiful white granite, expertly cut, and layered low as demarcators than as defenses. Zhang and Cui got out of the van after confirming their destination and walked for a bit, passing by a group of students and staff before halting at a great arch that served as the entrance to the university.

[list]

"What's this?" Cui inquired, staring up at the arch in awe. "This is... 50 meters at least."

"55 meters, good guess Comrade Cui." Zhang replied. "The students just call it Gate 1. It's officially known as the Hengzhi Gate though. It was constructed back in 2000 during the university's centennial. The designers were very precise too, they used 36500 white granite blocks to represent 36500 days, 100 years of the university's existence. Come on, let's get inside and I will show you what Kuanlo has been up to."

[/list]

After taking a moment to soak it all in, Cui Jin nodded and followed as Zhang walked through the Arc and into the university, disappearing behind a sea of further bureaucratic checkpoints.[/spoiler]

The sudden appearance of a foreign fleet of military ships would certainly be startling to both the government of Elesyr and its armed forces. The ships upon arriving at dock would be ordered by the naval command of the port (or Port Authority) to remain on standby until the right people had been called, namely those bigwigs in the Department of War and those in the government who had the pay and authority to hold diplomatic meetings. After about an hour of frantic calls and calmly worded orders in reply, the Steward of the Royal House would in acting as the right hand of the Emperor, permit the group on the ships to land formally on the dock.
